submission.justification: Module-D1 gives the highest light collection (50.9 PE/MeV at 30%), but in thermal-cycling tests 30% of D1 modules failed because the light-guide bonding cracked. The limit is 5%, and modules cannot be reached once the cryostat is filled, so D1 does not meet the robustness constraint. Of the robust designs, D2 (2% failures) collects much more light than D3 (35.6 vs 23.8 PE/MeV at 30%). Light collection rises with coverage, and the feedthroughs support up to 30%, so 30% coverage gives the most light. The cost of choosing D2 is about 30% less light than D1 would give.

requirements.evidence: D2 at 30% gives 35.6 PE/MeV, the highest of the designs that pass the robustness test (D3 gives 23.8). D1 would give 50.9 but fails robustness.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
Modules must be robust (inaccessible after fill)
requirements.evidence: thermal_cycling_tests.md: D2 had 2% failures after 20 cycles; the requirement is 5% or less. D1 had 30% and was rejected.
30% is the upper limit; the meeting notes confirm there are enough feedthroughs for 30%.
